inclusion.I1: Empirical English language MRI studies assessing grey matter (GM) volume differences between PTSD patients and controls
inclusion.I2: Whole-brain evidence- The paper must report at least one whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast of PTSD patients vs controls comparing GM volume
inclusion.I3: It is acceptable for qualifying results to be reported in tables of coordinates, figures, or supplementary materials when the main text clearly indicates those results are available.
inclusion.I4: Control populations may be healthy individuals or trauma-exposed individuals without PTS

exclusion.E1: Studies that report only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results.
exclusion.E2: Non-empirical papers (e.g., reviews, meta-analyses, methods-only, simulations) without original human structural MRI data.
exclusion.E3: Studies about trauma or stressful life event studies not specifically measuring PTSD
exclusion.E4: Treatment and longitudinal studies without a qualifying between-group contrast of PTSD patients vs controls
exclusion.E5: Studies that report only within group results in PTSD patients without a qualifying between-group contrast of PTSD patients vs controls
exclusion.E6: Studies report only null results (i.e., no significant differences between PTSD patients and controls)

inclusion.GLOBAL_I1: Must be a voxelwise whole brain analysis of grey matter volume

exclusion.GLOBAL_E1: Region of interest (ROI) or small volume correction (SVC) analyses
exclusion.GLOBAL_E2: Analyses of other modalities (e.g., functional MRI, diffusion tensor imaging) or other structural measures
exclusion.GLOBAL_E3: Within group analyses that do not compare PTSD patients to controls
exclusion.GLOBAL_E4: Analyses of treatment effects or longitudinal changes

inclusion.INCREASED_GM_I1: Voxelwise whole-brain grey matter comparison between PTSD patients and controls, with a patients > controls contrast indicating increased grey matter in PTSD patients.

inclusion.DECREASED_GM_I1: Voxelwise whole-brain grey matter comparison between PTSD patients and controls, with a patients < controls contrast indicating reduced grey matter in PTSD patients.
